questions.question: Under section 3313.475, which kinds of school districts must adopt the new policy?
questions.notes: City, local, exempted village and joint vocational school districts.

questions.question: Does section 3326.11 now make STEM schools follow section 3313.475?
questions.notes: Yes: 3313.475 is inserted into the list STEM schools must comply with.

questions.question: Do college-preparatory boarding schools have to follow the new rule in section 3313.475?
questions.notes: Yes: 3313.475 is inserted into section 3328.24's list.

questions.question: Where does the bill add section 3313.475 to the list of laws community schools must follow?
questions.notes: Division (A)(11)(d) of section 3314.03.

questions.question: Who is the primary sponsor of S. B. No. 113?
questions.notes: Senator Brenner.

questions.question: What does the bill say about the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974?
questions.notes: Attendance and participation records go to the department, auditor of state and sponsor as permitted under FERPA (existing law).

questions.question: Which bills of the 135th General Assembly amended section 3326.11?
How long do school districts have to put the new rule in place?
questions.notes: Not later than ninety days after the section's effective date.

questions.question: Can a school just give its diversity office a new name and keep it going?
questions.notes: No: replacing a prohibited office under a different designation serving the same purposes is prohibited.

questions.question: If a parent thinks the school broke this rule, what can they do?
questions.notes: Submit a complaint; the board investigates and holds a fair and impartial hearing.

questions.question: Can schools hire outside companies to help hire or promote people based on race or gender?
questions.notes: No: contracting with consultants or third parties whose role is to promote admissions, hiring or promotion based on race, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression is prohibited.

questions.question: Can a school keep the diversity department it already has?
questions.notes: No: continuing existing DEI offices or departments is prohibited.

questions.question: Can staff still be required to take diversity training?
questions.notes: No: any orientation or training course regarding DEI is prohibited.

questions.question: Can job postings at a school mention diversity, equity, and inclusion?
questions.notes: No: using DEI in job descriptions is prohibited.

questions.question: How much can a community school pay its sponsor for oversight?
questions.notes: Not more than three per cent of the state operating payments the school receives (existing law).

questions.question: What is the smallest number of students a community school must serve, and for how many hours a year?
questions.notes: Twenty-five students for nine hundred twenty hours per school year (existing law).

questions.question: What happens if a new community school doesn't open by the end of September?
questions.notes: In its first year, the contract is void (unless it solely serves dropouts) (existing law).

questions.question: Which existing sections of the Revised Code does this bill repeal?
questions.notes: Repeal language (no struck text in this bill): existing sections 3314.03, 3326.11 and 3328.24, replaced by the amended versions.

questions.question: How much extra money will schools get to follow this rule?
questions.notes: The bill has no funding provisions.

questions.question: Does this bill change the rules for school lunches?
questions.notes: Not addressed.

questions.question: Does this bill change the rules for school sports teams?
questions.notes: Not addressed.
